title: YNX Integration and Founder Control
metaDescription: Central acceptance, protocol freeze, dependency order and public-proof control for the YNX Testnet product ecosystem.
summary: The Integration controller validates exact product commits and evidence. It does not replace product owners or treat candidate, preview, simulator, unsigned or test-signed outputs as production releases.
features: Exact Git source and owner-evidence validation
Cross-product happy and fail-closed Testnet vectors
risks: Seven protected source candidates are centrally accepted: Chain Core, Wallet/Auth, Economics, Oracle, Data Fabric, Security/SRE and Governance. The other 29 products and shared-Testnet proof remain incomplete.
A Website page is not evidence that a product runtime is publicly deployed.
Testnet acceptance does not authorize Mainnet, production signing or store release.

faq.question: Does Integration implement every YNX product?
faq.answer: No. Product owners implement their products. Integration accepts only exact, source-bound contracts, tests, artifacts and public evidence.

faq.question: Does a successful preview mean a product is publicly released?
faq.answer: No. Preview, simulator, unsigned, test-signed, staging, public runtime, production signing and store release are separate states.

faq.question: Does Testnet acceptance promote Mainnet?
faq.answer: No. Mainnet is a separate later gate with independent security, governance, signer, funding and public evidence.
